question.problem: Expressed as a nonnegative integer smaller than $33,$ the additive inverse of $17$ modulo $33$ is{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
The additive inverse of $17$ modulo $33$ is the integer $0\le x<33$ such that

$$
x+17≡0\,(\text{mod}\,33).
$$

Notice that $-17+17≡0,$ so $x≡-17\,(\text{mod}\,33).$ To write this in the required form, we use the following sequence of congruences:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ≡-17 & \,(\text{mod}\,33) \\  & ≡0-17 & \,(\text{mod}\,33) \\  & ≡33-17 & \,(\text{mod}\,33) \\  & ≡16 & \,(\text{mod}\,33)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the additive inverse of the element $17$ modulo $33$ is $16.$

We can verify this result as follows:

$$
16+17≡33≡0\,\,✓\,(\text{mod}\,33)
$$

**Note:** The additive inverse of $a$ modulo $n$ is simply the residue of $-a$ modulo $n,$ i.e. $-a\,\text{mod}\,n.$
